title: Round inside square leaves corners
hook: Which shape leaves unused corners in this square space?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: The inscribed circle touches all four sides yet occupies less area than the square. Corner gaps remain outside the circular footprint; touching the sides is not the same as filling the region.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.

recall.question: A round tin 30 cm across sits in a 30 × 30 cm square space, touching all four sides. About what share of the square is left in the corners?
options: None: it touches all four sides
recall.why: The square is 900 cm²; the circle is π × 15² ≈ 707 cm². About 193 cm², roughly 21%, sits in the corners. Touching the sides is not filling the space.
